summary: A 30-minute coaching 1-1 between sales manager Chris Klevan and closer Andrew Musial (Fathom label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)'), opening on the tail of a group call with Ben Byrne. Chris reviews a recorded price-drop from one of Andrew's lost deals, criticises it as stilted and 'manufactured', and drills the scripted transition repeatedly until Andrew delivers it naturally. The pricing coached is consistent with the standard offer: '12 months for 9K or six months for 6K'. The back half covers objection philosophy — treating 'I need to think about it' as fear, isolating finances, and using certainty language — plus how to behave while a prospect is entering payment details.
notable: Manager coaches the rep to keep prospects conversationally occupied while they are entering financing details, explicitly to stop them reconsidering: 'keeping them talking so they're busy... so that way they'll just keep going through.'

Andrew references a prior prospect with 'stage three or four cancer' who backed out. The condition is discussed only as evidence that money is a psychological rather than real obstacle; no clinical screening or clearance is mentioned by either party.
Two of Andrew's deposits had to be refunded ('So did both of your deposits need to be refunded?' / 'Yeah'), confirming a deposit-then-refund practice is in live use.
Standard pricing restated correctly and repeatedly by the manager as 6K/6mo and 9K/12mo — this call is the cleanest internal confirmation of the official price ladder.
Chris frames non-buyers fatalistically: 'if they end up dying for the pattern in this lifetime, they'll get another chance at some point.'
The rep appears throughout the 'Andrew Musial' folder under the Fathom display name 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)'.
